27.layer4_ar: يُجلِّل الفريقان الشيعي والسني النبيَّ إبراهيم عليه السلام ويُقرَّان بالنسل المبارك الذي انحدر منه. ويُؤكِّد كلٌّ من ابن كثير والطباطبائي أن النبوة استمرَّت في ذرية إبراهيم عليه السلام لتبلغ ذروتها في النبي محمد صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم الخاتم. وثمة إجماعٌ على أن إبراهيم عليه السلام نال في الدنيا والآخرة جزاءً يليق بوفائه. وإنما يقع الاختلاف في تحديد بعض الذرية؛ فالتقليد الشيعي يُلحِق في هذا النسل المبارك أئمةَ أهل البيت عليهم السلام المنحدرين من النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم، في حين يختلف التقليد السني في فهم السلطة الدينية بعد النبي. ويتَّفق الفريقان على أن إسحاق ويعقوب عليهما السلام من أنبياء نسل إبراهيم. ويُلاحِظ المفسِّرون الكلاسيكيون من الفريقَين أن الآية تُجسِّد العدل الإلهي والكرم الإلهي في مكافأة من يتضحُّون في سبيل الله. ويُناقش الرازي العطاء الإلهي والعدالة الإلهية بأسلوبٍ مقارب لما عند الطباطبائي. ويُؤكِّد الفريقان أن الذرية الصالحة من أجلِّ النعم الإلهية، وينطلقان من هذه الآية لتأكيد أهمية التنشئة الحسنة للأبناء. ويستشهد علماء الفريقَين المعاصرون بهذه الآية في الحديث عن أهمية الأسرة وتنشئة الأجيال الصالحة ومبدأ أن الوفاء لله يُثمر جزاءً شاملاً. ويرى الفريقان في مثال إبراهيم عليه السلام دافعًا يحثُّ المؤمنين على التضحية من أجل الإيمان ثقةً بالحكمة الإلهية وسعة الكرم الإلهي.
27.layer1: Verse 27 of Surah Al-Ankabut records Allah's magnificent reward to Ibrahim following his migration and steadfastness in faith. Having left everything behind for Allah's sake, Ibrahim received in this world what no wealth or kingdom could have purchased: a blessed posterity carrying prophethood and divine scripture across generations. Allah says He granted Ibrahim 'Ishaq wa-Yaqoub' — Isaac and Jacob — and placed in his offspring both the institution of prophethood (al-nubuwwah) and the gift of scripture (al-kitab). Isaac was Ibrahim's son through Sarah, born miraculously in old age, and Jacob was Isaac's son. Through this lineage came an unbroken chain of prophets: David, Solomon, Moses, Jesus, and ultimately — through the line of Ismail, Ibrahim's other son — Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him all. The verse then adds that Ibrahim received his reward in this world, and in the Hereafter he is among the righteous. Scholars explain that the worldly reward encompasses righteous offspring, prophetic legacy, universal honor among believers of every faith tradition, and the lasting remembrance that continues to this day. This verse teaches several profound lessons: that sacrifice for Allah is never in vain, that divine compensation often exceeds what was sacrificed, that the greatest inheritance one can leave is not property but righteousness and prophetic guidance, and that a person's impact through faith can extend across centuries and civilizations. For believing parents today, this verse is a reminder that raising righteous children and instilling faith in the family is among the highest acts of worship — one whose rewards ripple through generations far beyond one's own lifetime.
27.layer2: Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir al-Quran al-Azim explains that the granting of Isaac and Jacob to Ibrahim came as a direct consequence of his sincere migration and steadfast worship. He notes that the phrase 'We placed in his offspring prophethood and scripture' is among the most comprehensive divine gifts recorded in the Quran, encompassing every revealed book — the Torah, Psalms, Gospel, and Quran — and every prophet sent after Ibrahim. Ibn Kathir draws attention to the fact that among Ibrahim's descendants through Isaac, prophethood continued uninterruptedly through the Israelite prophets, while the line through Ismail culminated in the final prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him. Imam Tabari in his Jami al-Bayan traces the chain of prophets flowing from Ibrahim's lineage: Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Moses, Aaron, David, Solomon, Zachariah, John, and Jesus through the Israelite line, and Muhammad through the Ishmaelite line — a demonstration of how Allah fulfilled His promise to Ibrahim on a scale that exceeds human imagination. Imam al-Qurtubi discusses the statement 'his reward in this world' and identifies multiple components: righteous progeny, long life with blessing, the universal love that believers of every religion bear for Ibrahim, and the special honor of being designated khalilullah — the intimate friend of Allah — a title found nowhere else in the Quran. Fakhr al-Din al-Razi in his Mafatih al-Ghayb reflects on the theological significance of combining worldly and heavenly reward in the same verse, arguing that it refutes the view of those who claim that true piety requires total deprivation in this life and that proper alignment with Allah's will naturally draws divine blessing in both realms.
27.layer3: Sayyid Qutb in Fi Zilal al-Quran treats verse 27 as the Quranic proof that faith is never a dead end — it is always an opening. Ibrahim gave up a homeland and people who rejected him, and Allah gave him in return a homeland of the spirit that encompasses all of humanity's prophetic tradition. Qutb writes that the divine equation is always just and always generous: what a believer sacrifices for Allah is returned multiplied, purified, and lasting. Wahbah al-Zuhayli in Al-Tafsir al-Munir connects this verse to the broader Quranic pattern of divine response to sincere sacrifice, noting that throughout the Quran, every prophet who gave up worldly security for truth received divine compensation that vastly exceeded his material loss — a pattern meant to encourage believers across all times who face the same choice. Contemporary Islamic scholar Muhammad al-Ghazali, in his thematic analysis of the Quran, observes that the placement of prophetic lineage as Ibrahim's greatest worldly reward reflects a Quranic value system in which human impact through faith dwarfs all material achievement: Ibrahim had no kingdom to show for his life, but every mosque, every call to prayer, and every act of monotheistic worship across three of the world's major religions traces back to his legacy. Practically, Ibn Uthaymeen emphasizes in his lessons that the verse teaches believers to invest in the spiritual formation of their children and communities, trusting that such investment — though invisible in material terms — creates the most enduring legacy. The concluding statement that Ibrahim is among the righteous in the Hereafter confirms that divine reward is not exhausted by worldly blessings but continues into eternity.

concepts.title: Unprecedented Sin
concepts.coreInsight: Lot's people committed immorality unprecedented in human history, showing how societies can normalize what was once unthinkable.
concepts.whyItMatters: Moral boundaries matter - what begins as deviation can become widespread corruption if not challenged by voices of conscience.
concepts.arabicHighlight: إِنَّكُمْ لَتَأْتُونَ ٱلْفَٰحِشَةَ مَا سَبَقَكُم بِهَا مِنْ أَحَدٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: لوط کے لوگوں نے انسانی تاریخ میں بے مثال بے حیائی کی، جو ظاہر کرتا ہے کہ معاشرے کیسے ایسی چیزوں کو عام بنا سکتے ہیں جو کبھی ناقابل تصور تھیں۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: اخلاقی حدود اہمیت رکھتی ہیں - جو انحراف سے شروع ہوتا ہے وہ وسیع پیمانے پر بدعنوانی بن سکتا ہے اگر ضمیر کی آوازوں کے ذریعے چیلنج نہ کیا جائے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: ارتكب قوم لوط فحشاء غير مسبوقة في تاريخ البشرية، مما يظهر كيف يمكن للمجتمعات أن تطبع ما كان غير متصور يوماً.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: الحدود الأخلاقية مهمة - ما يبدأ كانحراف يمكن أن يصبح فساداً واسع النطاق إذا لم يتحداه أصوات الضمير.

concepts.title: Prophet's Warning
concepts.coreInsight: Lot fulfilled his prophetic duty by directly confronting societal sins, despite knowing it would bring rejection and hostility.
concepts.whyItMatters: Speaking truth to power and confronting injustice is a religious duty, even when it's unpopular or dangerous.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: لوط نے سماجی گناہوں کا براہ راست مقابلہ کرکے اپنا نبوی فرض پورا کیا، حالانکہ وہ جانتے تھے کہ یہ مسترد ہونے اور دشمنی لائے گا۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: طاقت کے سامنے سچ بولنا اور ناانصافی کا مقابلہ کرنا مذہبی فرض ہے، چاہے یہ غیر مقبول یا خطرناک ہو۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: أدى لوط واجبه النبوي بمواجهة خطايا المجتمع مباشرة، رغم علمه أنه سيجلب الرفض والعداء.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: قول الحقيقة للسلطة ومواجهة الظلم واجب ديني، حتى عندما يكون غير شعبي أو خطير.

concepts.title: Global First
concepts.coreInsight: The phrase 'from among the worlds' emphasizes this was not just local deviance but a historical first across all civilizations.
concepts.whyItMatters: Understanding historical context helps us recognize when societies cross dangerous moral thresholds that previous generations avoided.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: جملہ 'عالمین میں سے' اس بات پر زور دیتا ہے کہ یہ صرف مقامی انحراف نہیں بلکہ تمام تہذیبوں میں تاریخی پہلا واقعہ تھا۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: تاریخی سیاق و سباق کو سمجھنا ہمیں پہچانے میں مدد کرتا ہے کہ کب معاشرے خطرناک اخلاقی حدوں کو عبور کرتے ہیں جن سے پچھلی نسلیں بچتی تھیں۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: عبارة 'من العالمين' تؤكد أن هذا لم يكن مجرد انحراف محلي بل أول حدث تاريخي عبر جميع الحضارات.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: فهم السياق التاريخي يساعدنا على التعرف على متى تعبر المجتمعات عتبات أخلاقية خطيرة تجنبتها الأجيال السابقة.

28.layer4: Both Shia and Sunni scholars unanimously agree that this verse condemns homosexual practice. Ibn Kathir and Tabatabai both explain that the people of Lot committed an unprecedented sexual sin. There is scholarly consensus across all Islamic legal schools that homosexual acts are prohibited. Classical exegetes across traditions emphasize the severity of this sin based on this verse and the subsequent punishment of Lot's people. Both traditions teach that sexual relations are permitted only within marriage between man and woman. Some difference exists in specific legal penalties prescribed in Islamic law, with variation among schools of jurisprudence, but all agree on the basic prohibition. Contemporary scholars across traditions face challenges in maintaining traditional Islamic teaching in contexts where homosexuality is accepted or celebrated. There is common ground in distinguishing between the person, who deserves dignity and respect, and the act, which is sinful. Both traditions emphasize that Islamic sexual ethics serve divine wisdom and human flourishing. Al-Razi discusses the wisdom of sexual regulations in ways comparable to Shia scholars. While some modernist Muslim voices have attempted to reinterpret these verses, classical and mainstream contemporary scholarship in both traditions maintains the clear condemnation of homosexual practice as established in Quran and hadith.
28.layer4_urdu: شیعہ اور سنی دونوں علماء متفقہ طور پر اس بات پر متفق ہیں کہ یہ آیت اس مخصوص عمل کی مذمت کرتی ہے۔ ابن کثیر اور طباطبائی دونوں وضاحت کرتے ہیں کہ حضرت لوط کی قوم نے ایک بے مثال جنسی گناہ کیا۔ تمام اسلامی فقہی مکاتب میں علمی اتفاق ہے کہ یہ اعمال حرام ہیں۔ تمام روایات کے کلاسیکی مفسرین اس آیت اور حضرت لوط کی قوم کی بعد کی سزا کی بنیاد پر اس گناہ کی شدت پر زور دیتے ہیں۔ دونوں روایات تعلیم دیتی ہیں کہ جنسی تعلقات صرف مرد اور عورت کے درمیان نکاح میں جائز ہیں۔ اسلامی قانون میں مقرر کردہ مخصوص قانونی سزاؤں میں کچھ فرق موجود ہے، فقہی مکاتب میں اختلاف کے ساتھ، لیکن سب بنیادی ممانعت پر متفق ہیں۔ عصری علماء تمام روایات میں چیلنجوں کا سامنا کرتے ہیں روایتی اسلامی تعلیم کو برقرار رکھنے میں ایسے سیاق و سباق میں جہاں اس طرز عمل کو قبول یا منایا جاتا ہے۔ شخص، جو وقار اور احترام کا مستحق ہے، اور عمل، جو گناہ ہے، میں فرق کرنے میں مشترکہ بنیاد ہے۔ دونوں روایات زور دیتی ہیں کہ اسلامی جنسی اخلاقیات الہٰی حکمت اور انسانی فلاح کی خدمت کرتی ہیں۔ الرازی نے جنسی ضوابط کی حکمت پر اسی طرح بحث کی جیسے شیعہ علماء نے۔ اگرچہ کچھ جدید پسند مسلم آوازوں نے ان آیات کی دوبارہ تشریح کی کوشش کی ہے، لیکن کلاسیکی اور مرکزی دھارے کی عصری علمیت دونوں روایات میں قرآن اور حدیث میں قائم شدہ اس عمل کی واضح ممانعت کو برقرار رکھتی ہے۔
28.layer4_ar: يتَّفق علماء الشيعة والسنة على أن هذه الآية تُدين الممارسات الجنسية المثلية إدانةً قاطعة؛ فكلٌّ من ابن كثير والطباطبائي يُبيِّن أن قوم لوط ارتكبوا جريمةً جنسية غير مسبوقة. وثمة إجماعٌ علمي في المذاهب الإسلامية كلِّها على تحريم الأفعال الجنسية المثلية. ويُشدِّد المفسِّرون الكلاسيكيون من الفريقَين على خطورة هذا الانحراف استنادًا إلى هذه الآية وما أعقبها من العذاب. ويُقرِّر الفريقان أن العلاقات الجنسية المشروعة لا تكون إلا في إطار الزواج بين رجلٍ وامرأة. وإنما يقع التمايز في العقوبات الفقهية المقرَّرة، وهي مسألةٌ خلافية بين المذاهب الفقهية المختلفة، مع الاتفاق على أصل التحريم. ويواجه علماء الفريقَين المعاصرون تحديًا في الدفاع عن الموقف الإسلامي في سياقاتٍ باتت المثلية مقبولةً أو مُحتفَلًا بها. وثمة أرضية مشتركة في التمييز بين الشخص —الذي يستحق الكرامة والاحترام— وبين الفعل الذي يُعدُّ إثمًا. ويُؤكِّد الفريقان أن الأخلاق الجنسية الإسلامية تخدم الحكمة الإلهية والازدهار الإنساني. ويناقش الرازي مقاصد الضوابط الجنسية بما يتوافق مع مقاربات العلماء الشيعة. وفي حين حاول بعض الأصوات التحديثية إعادة تأويل هذه الآيات، يُبقي الاتجاه العلمي الكلاسيكي والمعاصر السائد في الفريقَين على إدانة الممارسات الجنسية المثلية بوصفها ثابتةً في القرآن والسنة.
28.layer1: Verse 28 introduces the story of Prophet Lot and his prophetic mission to the people of Sodom, a city near the Dead Sea in the region of ancient Palestine. Following his migration with Ibrahim from Iraq to Syria, Lot was sent as a Messenger to a community whose moral corruption had reached a level previously unrecorded in human history. The verse quotes his direct address to his people: 'Indeed, you approach men with desire, instead of women. Rather, you are a transgressing people.' The Arabic word 'fahisha' — translated as indecency or obscenity — carries a strong connotation of something that is both shameful and universally recognized as wrong. The phrase 'ma sabaqakum biha min ahadin min al-alamin' — 'such as none preceding you among the worlds has done' — emphasizes the absolute novelty of this practice in human history. This statement serves several functions in the surah's broader argument: it connects to the opening theme of trials and the testing of communities, it provides a concrete example of how societies can descend into unprecedented levels of transgression, and it demonstrates Lot's prophetic courage in naming and confronting a sin that had been normalized and even celebrated by his community. The word 'musrifun' at the verse's end — often translated as 'transgressors' or 'those who exceed all bounds' — captures the idea of going beyond every natural and divine limit. This verse sets the stage for understanding Lot's lonely struggle: he was one voice of conscience inside a society that had collectively abandoned not only divine law but basic human norms, making his mission among the most difficult faced by any prophet in the Quranic narrative.
28.layer2: Imam Tabari in his Jami al-Bayan narrates from multiple chains of transmission that Lot was the son of Ibrahim's brother Haran, making him Ibrahim's nephew. He was sent as a prophet specifically to the people of Sodom and the surrounding cities, which are identified in various traditions as five cities, four of which were destroyed while the fifth was spared because its inhabitants had not participated in the transgression. Tabari records from Ibn Abbas that when Lot confronted his people with this indecency, he was the first prophet to face this particular challenge, there being no precedent for such an open communal practice of sodomy in any nation before them. Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir al-Quran al-Azim quotes the famous statement that none of the nations before the people of Lot had engaged in this practice collectively and openly, citing early authorities including Mujahid and Qatada, who confirm the novelty of their transgression. Al-Qurtubi in Al-Jami li-Ahkam al-Quran uses this verse as the foundational Quranic evidence for the prohibition of sodomy in Islamic law, noting that the Quran's own characterization of the act as 'fahisha' — a major obscenity — establishes the legal basis for its prohibition independent of any specific hadith. He notes that all four schools of Islamic jurisprudence — Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i, and Hanbali — unanimously prohibit the act, though they differ on the specific punishment. The Quranic phrase 'none among the worlds' is analyzed by al-Razi as referring to all human civilizations that existed before the people of Lot, establishing the historical and universal character of Lot's condemnation.
28.layer3: Contemporary Sunni scholars have addressed this verse in the context of modern debates about sexual ethics and religious authority. Wahbah al-Zuhayli in Al-Tafsir al-Munir maintains that the Quranic condemnation in this verse and in other passages dealing with the people of Lot is unambiguous and binding, representing a divinely established moral norm that cannot be altered by changing social conditions. He emphasizes that Lot's courage in naming the transgression publicly, despite being outnumbered and facing ridicule, is itself a prophetic model for Muslim communities facing social pressure to normalize what Islam prohibits. Sayyid Qutb in Fi Zilal al-Quran draws attention to the Quranic language of 'transgressing all bounds' as pointing to a deeper spiritual principle: moral corruption rarely remains isolated but tends to overflow into every dimension of social life, as subsequent verses about the same community will demonstrate. Ibn Uthaymeen, in his treatment of prophetic stories in the Quran, observes that Lot's statement 'none among the worlds' is not hyperbole but a factual assessment confirmed by the Quran itself, and he uses it to address Muslims who might be tempted to accommodate contemporary social trends in religious teaching, arguing that the Quranic standard is eternal and cannot be revised. From a social analysis perspective, contemporary scholars note that verse 28 prefigures the broader sociological pattern described in verses 29-30: once a community normalizes one category of transgression, other forms of lawlessness and moral chaos typically follow, a pattern visible in the subsequent descriptions of robbery, public obscenity, and contemptuous rejection of divine warning.

concepts.title: Public Shamelessness
concepts.coreInsight: The people committed evil openly in their gatherings, showing how moral decline leads to shamelessness and public celebration of sin.
concepts.whyItMatters: When society stops being ashamed of wrongdoing and begins celebrating it publicly, it signals deep moral corruption.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: لوگوں نے اپنی مجلسوں میں کھلے عام برائی کی، جو ظاہر کرتا ہے کہ اخلاقی زوال کیسے بے شرمی اور گناہ کے عوامی جشن کی طرف لے جاتا ہے۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: جب معاشرہ غلط کام سے شرمندہ ہونا چھوڑ دیتا ہے اور اسے عوامی طور پر منانا شروع کر دیتا ہے، تو یہ گہری اخلاقی خرابی کی علامت ہے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: ارتكب الناس الشر علناً في تجمعاتهم، مما يظهر كيف يؤدي التدهور الأخلاقي إلى الوقاحة والاحتفال العام بالخطيئة.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: عندما يتوقف المجتمع عن الخجل من الأعمال السيئة ويبدأ في الاحتفال بها علناً، فهذا يشير إلى فساد أخلاقي عميق.

concepts.title: Cut the Road
concepts.coreInsight: They obstructed roads, showing how moral corruption extends to economic crimes and creating an environment of lawlessness.
concepts.whyItMatters: Sin rarely stays confined - moral decay in one area spreads to other aspects of society, affecting safety and livelihoods.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: انہوں نے راستوں کو روک دیا، جو ظاہر کرتا ہے کہ اخلاقی بدعنوانی کیسے معاشی جرائم تک پھیلتی ہے اور بےقانونی کا ماحول پیدا کرتی ہے۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: گناہ شاذ و نادر ہی محدود رہتا ہے - ایک شعبے میں اخلاقی زوال معاشرے کے دوسرے پہلوؤں تک پھیلتا ہے، حفاظت اور روزی روٹی کو متاثر کرتا ہے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: عرقلوا الطرق، مما يظهر كيف يمتد الفساد الأخلاقي إلى الجرائم الاقتصادية وخلق بيئة من الفوضى.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: نادراً ما تبقى الخطيئة محصورة - التدهور الأخلاقي في منطقة ينتشر إلى جوانب أخرى من المجتمع، مما يؤثر على السلامة وسبل العيش.

concepts.title: Mocking Challenge
concepts.coreInsight: Instead of repenting, they arrogantly challenged Lot to bring Allah's punishment, showing extreme hardness of heart.
concepts.whyItMatters: Arrogance and mockery in response to divine warnings indicate a dangerous spiritual state that precedes divine punishment.
concepts.arabicHighlight: ٱئْتِنَا بِعَذَابِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: توبہ کرنے کے بجائے، انہوں نے گھمنڈ سے لوط کو چیلنج کیا کہ اللہ کا عذاب لاؤ، جو انتہائی سخت دلی کو ظاہر کرتا ہے۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: الہٰی تنبیہات کے جواب میں تکبر اور تمسخر ایک خطرناک روحانی حالت کی نشاندہی کرتے ہیں جو الہٰی عذاب سے پہلے آتی ہے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: بدلاً من التوبة، تحدوا لوط بغطرسة ليجلب عذاب الله، مما يظهر قسوة قلب شديدة.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: الغطرسة والسخرية رداً على التحذيرات الإلهية تشير إلى حالة روحية خطيرة تسبق العذاب الإلهي.

29.layer4: Both Shia and Sunni exegetes agree that this verse describes comprehensive corruption in the society of Lot. Ibn Kathir provides details about the specific sins comparable to those in Shia sources. There is consensus that cutting off the road refers to highway robbery and that committing evil in assemblies indicates shamelessness. Classical scholars across traditions emphasize that public sin is more harmful than private sin because it corrupts the entire social environment. Both traditions teach that the people's mocking challenge demonstrated arrogance and brought swift punishment. Al-Razi discusses the relationship between different forms of corruption in ways similar to Tabatabai. There is common ground in teaching that loss of shame regarding sin is a dangerous sign of moral decline. Both traditions cite hadith about the obligation to forbid evil publicly and the consequences when societies fail to do so. Contemporary scholars across traditions address the tension between Islamic moral teaching and modern cultures that celebrate behaviors Islam condemns. There is consensus that Muslims must maintain moral conviction and avoid participating in or celebrating what Islam prohibits, while treating all people with respect. Both traditions warn that societies that openly mock divine moral law invite divine judgment, while calling believers to wisdom and compassion in calling people to righteousness.
29.layer4_urdu: شیعہ اور سنی دونوں مفسرین اس بات پر متفق ہیں کہ یہ آیت حضرت لوط کے معاشرے میں جامع فساد کو بیان کرتی ہے۔ ابن کثیر نے شیعہ ذرائع میں موجود مخصوص گناہوں کے بارے میں قابل موازنہ تفصیلات فراہم کیں۔ اس بات پر اتفاق ہے کہ راستہ کاٹنا شاہراہ ڈاکوزنی کا حوالہ دیتا ہے اور محفلوں میں برائی کرنا بے شرمی کی نشاندہی کرتا ہے۔ تمام روایات کے کلاسیکی علماء زور دیتے ہیں کہ عوامی گناہ نجی گناہ سے زیادہ نقصان دہ ہے کیونکہ یہ پورے سماجی ماحول کو خراب کرتا ہے۔ دونوں روایات تعلیم دیتی ہیں کہ لوگوں کا مذاق میں چیلنج تکبر کو ظاہر کرتا تھا اور فوری سزا لائی۔ الرازی نے مختلف اقسام کے فساد کے درمیان تعلق پر اسی طرح بحث کی جیسے طباطبائی نے۔ گناہ کے بارے میں شرم کے کھو جانے کو اخلاقی زوال کی خطرناک علامت ہونے کی تعلیم میں مشترکہ بنیاد ہے۔ دونوں روایات احادیث کا حوالہ دیتی ہیں برائی کو کھلے عام منع کرنے کی ذمہ داری کے بارے میں اور اس کے نتائج جب معاشرے ایسا کرنے میں ناکام ہوں۔ عصری علماء تمام روایات میں اسلامی اخلاقی تعلیم اور جدید ثقافتوں کے درمیان تناؤ سے نمٹتے ہیں جو اسلام جن طرز عمل کی مذمت کرتا ہے انہیں مناتی ہیں۔ اس بات پر اتفاق ہے کہ مسلمانوں کو اخلاقی یقین برقرار رکھنا چاہیے اور جو اسلام حرام کرتا ہے اس میں شرکت یا تعریف سے بچنا چاہیے، جبکہ تمام لوگوں کے ساتھ احترام سے پیش آنا چاہیے۔ دونوں روایات خبردار کرتی ہیں کہ معاشرے جو کھلے عام الہٰی اخلاقی قانون کا مذاق اڑاتے ہیں الہٰی فیصلے کو دعوت دیتے ہیں، جبکہ مومنوں کو لوگوں کو نیکی کی طرف بلانے میں حکمت اور ہمدردی کی دعوت دیتے ہیں۔
29.layer4_ar: يتَّفق المفسِّرون الشيعة والسنة على أن هذه الآية تصف فسادًا شاملاً متعدِّد الأوجه في قوم لوط عليه السلام. ويُقدِّم ابن كثير تفاصيلَ عن ذنوبهم المتنوِّعة تتقارب مع ما في المصادر الشيعية. وثمة إجماعٌ على أن «قطع السبيل» يُشير إلى النهب وقطع الطريق، وأن ارتكاب المنكرات في المجالس يُفيد انعدام الحياء. ويُشدِّد علماء كلا التقليدَين على أن الذنوب العلنية أشدُّ ضررًا من الذنوب السرِّية لما تُحدِثه من تلوُّثٍ في البيئة الاجتماعية برمَّتها. ويُقرِّر الفريقان أن تحدِّي القوم لنبيِّهم يكشف عن عجرفةٍ أجلبت عليهم العقوبة العاجلة. ويُناقش الرازي العلاقةَ بين صنوف الفساد المختلفة بأسلوبٍ مماثل للطباطبائي. وثمة أرضية مشتركة في تعليم أن انعدام الحياء من الذنب علامةٌ خطيرة على الانهيار الأخلاقي. ويستشهد الفريقان بالأحاديث التي توجِب الإنكار العلني للمنكر وتُحذِّر من تبعات التقاعس عنه. ويتناول علماء الفريقَين المعاصرون التوتُّرَ القائم بين الموقف الإسلامي والثقافات الحديثة التي تُكرِّم ما يُحرِّمه الإسلام. وثمة إجماعٌ على أن المسلمين مُلزَمون بصون قناعتهم الأخلاقية والامتناع عن المشاركة في ما يُحرِّمه الإسلام أو الاحتفاء به، مع معاملة جميع الناس باحترام. ويُحذِّر الفريقان من أن المجتمعات التي تستهزئ علنًا بالشريعة الأخلاقية الإلهية تستدعي حكم الله، داعِيَين المؤمنين إلى الحكمة والرحمة في دعوة الناس إلى الحق.
29.layer1: Verse 29 presents Lot's comprehensive indictment of his people, cataloguing three distinct forms of transgression that had taken root in Sodom. He challenges them: 'Do you indeed approach men, and cut off the road, and commit in your assemblies the worst of evil deeds?' This three-part accusation reveals how deeply corruption had penetrated every dimension of community life. The first charge references the same sexual transgression mentioned in verse 28, confirming that Lot's confrontation was consistent and repeated. The second charge — 'cutting off the road' — is interpreted by classical scholars in two main ways: either literal highway robbery that made the region dangerous for travelers, or a broader metaphor for blocking the path to truth and righteousness. Many scholars accept both meanings simultaneously. The third charge — 'committing evil deeds in your assemblies' — refers to open and shameless public transgression, in the very gatherings that should have been spaces for social virtue and mutual accountability. Ibn Abbas is reported to have said that their assemblies were sites of the worst kinds of behavior, committed without any sense of shame or restraint. The people's response is recorded in the same verse: 'Bring us Allah's punishment, if you should be of the truthful.' This arrogant challenge — essentially daring Allah to punish them — represents the final stage of moral hardening: not simply rejecting the message but actively taunting the messenger and mocking divine justice. The verse thus shows a community that had moved beyond indifference into active hostility toward truth, a pattern that the Quran consistently identifies as the threshold beyond which divine punishment becomes inevitable.
29.layer2: Imam Tabari records from Ibn Abbas and others that 'cutting off the road' referred to multiple practices simultaneously: the people of Sodom would waylay travelers, rob them, and also subject them to the same sexual violation they committed against residents, making the roads surrounding their cities extremely dangerous. Some narrations indicate that they would assault travelers publicly, without shame. Tabari also notes scholarly discussion about what 'evil deeds in your assemblies' specifically refers to, preserving opinions that range from passing wind and breaking social norms as a deliberate act of provocation, to public sexual acts, to collective mocking and abusing of Lot and his small group of believers. Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir al-Quran al-Azim draws on a narration from Ibn Abbas preserved in the books of tafsir — though he notes it is unusual — that the people of Lot would commit obscene acts openly in their gatherings with neither modesty nor concealment, which is understood as part of the normalization of their transgression. More importantly, Ibn Kathir emphasizes the people's response as a sign of their spiritual destruction: asking for the punishment to come was not an act of doubt about Lot's prophecy but of contempt for it. Al-Qurtubi analyzes the verse as illustrating a pattern found elsewhere in the Quran — for example in the story of Noah and the story of Salih — where a people's crimes escalate and their rejection of the prophet becomes increasingly bold until divine punishment follows. Fakhr al-Din al-Razi uses this verse to explore the social psychology of corruption: when sin becomes public and celebrated, the last barriers of individual conscience dissolve, and collective transgression reaches a qualitative threshold that invites divine response.
29.layer3: Sayyid Qutb in Fi Zilal al-Quran offers a penetrating analysis of the three crimes mentioned in verse 29 as representing three dimensions of social disintegration: the corruption of natural human relationships through sexual transgression, the destruction of public safety and economic trust through highway robbery, and the erosion of the communal conscience through shameless public sinning. He argues that when a society celebrates transgression in its very gathering spaces — its public squares, entertainment venues, and cultural events — it has reached a terminal stage of moral collapse. Wahbah al-Zuhayli notes that the verse's enumeration of multiple simultaneous crimes reflects the Quranic principle that immorality is never contained but spreads and deepens over time, each violation weakening the social fabric that might otherwise check the next. The people's demand — 'Bring us Allah's punishment' — is analyzed by contemporary scholars as the ultimate expression of what Islamic ethics calls kibr (arrogance), the spiritual disease that makes a person impervious to divine guidance. Ibn Uthaymeen observes that this verse should prompt believers to reflect on whether their own communities and gathering places reflect values that honor divine guidance or gradually normalize what Allah has prohibited, noting that the descent into the condition described here does not happen suddenly but through incremental accommodation of increasingly serious wrongs. Modern scholars also draw from this verse lessons about the obligation of individuals to maintain conscience and voice within communities facing moral decline, noting that Lot's continued confrontation — documented repeatedly across this surah — models the prophetic duty to speak truth even when outnumbered and mocked.

concepts.title: Seeking Help
concepts.coreInsight: When all efforts failed, Lot turned to Allah in prayer, demonstrating the prophet's ultimate reliance on divine intervention.
concepts.whyItMatters: When human efforts prove insufficient against corruption, turning to Allah in sincere supplication is the believer's ultimate recourse.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: جب تمام کوششیں ناکام ہو گئیں، لوط نے دعا میں اللہ کی طرف رجوع کیا، جو نبی کی الہٰی مداخلت پر حتمی انحصار کو ظاہر کرتا ہے۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: جب انسانی کوششیں بدعنوانی کے خلاف ناکافی ثابت ہوں، تو خلوص نیت سے اللہ کی طرف رجوع کرنا مومن کا آخری سہارا ہے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: عندما فشلت كل الجهود، لجأ لوط إلى الله في الدعاء، مما يدل على اعتماد النبي النهائي على التدخل الإلهي.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: عندما تثبت الجهود البشرية عدم كفايتها ضد الفساد، فإن اللجوء إلى الله في الدعاء الصادق هو الملاذ الأخير للمؤمن.

concepts.title: The Corrupt
concepts.coreInsight: Lot identified them as 'corrupting people' (mufsideen) - those who spread corruption and destroy the moral fabric of society.
concepts.whyItMatters: Recognizing and naming corruption for what it is, is essential before seeking divine help to combat it.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: لوط نے انہیں 'فساد پھیلانے والے لوگ' (مفسدین) کے طور پر پہچانا - وہ جو فساد پھیلاتے ہیں اور معاشرے کے اخلاقی تانے بانے کو تباہ کرتے ہیں۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: فساد کو اس کی حقیقت سے پہچاننا اور نام دینا ضروری ہے اس کے خلاف الہٰی مدد طلب کرنے سے پہلے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: عرّفهم لوط بأنهم 'قوم مفسدون' - أولئك الذين ينشرون الفساد ويدمرون النسيج الأخلاقي للمجتمع.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: التعرف على الفساد وتسميته بما هو عليه أمر ضروري قبل طلب المساعدة الإلهية لمكافحته.

30.layer4: Both Shia and Sunni scholars emphasize Lot's prayer as demonstrating proper reliance on Allah when facing opposition. Ibn Kathir and Tabatabai both note that this prayer was answered with immediate divine intervention, angels being sent to destroy the corrupt society. There is consensus that the term mufsideen indicates those who spread corruption, making their sin social as well as personal. Classical exegetes across traditions praise Lot's patience in calling his people to reform and his ultimate appeal to Allah for judgment when they refused. Both traditions teach that prayer for support against oppressors is legitimate and often answered. Al-Razi discusses the power of prophetic prayer comparable to discussions in Shia sources. There is common ground in teaching that believers should combine patient efforts at reform with prayer for divine support and intervention. Both traditions emphasize that ultimate judgment belongs to Allah and that apparent victory of evil is temporary. Contemporary scholars across traditions encourage believers facing oppression or widespread corruption to maintain hope and to pray consistently for divine support. There is consensus that prayer is not passive resignation but active engagement of divine power, and that sincere supplication can bring divine intervention that changes seemingly impossible situations. Both traditions see Lot's brief prayer as a model of turning to Allah in moments of crisis and trusting in divine justice.
30.layer4_urdu: شیعہ اور سنی دونوں علماء حضرت لوط کی دعا پر زور دیتے ہیں کہ یہ مخالفت کا سامنا کرتے وقت اللہ پر مناسب انحصار کو ظاہر کرتی ہے۔ ابن کثیر اور طباطبائی دونوں نوٹ کرتے ہیں کہ یہ دعا فوری الہٰی مداخلت کے ساتھ قبول ہوئی، فرشتوں کو بھیجا گیا فاسد معاشرے کو تباہ کرنے کے لیے۔ اس بات پر اتفاق ہے کہ اصطلاح مفسدین ان لوگوں کی نشاندہی کرتی ہے جو فساد پھیلاتے ہیں، ان کے گناہ کو سماجی کے ساتھ ساتھ ذاتی بناتے ہوئے۔ تمام روایات کے کلاسیکی مفسرین حضرت لوط کے صبر کی تعریف کرتے ہیں اپنی قوم کو اصلاح کی طرف بلانے میں اور ان کی آخری اللہ سے فیصلے کی اپیل جب انہوں نے انکار کیا۔ دونوں روایات تعلیم دیتی ہیں کہ ظالموں کے خلاف مدد کے لیے دعا جائز ہے اور اکثر قبول ہوتی ہے۔ الرازی نے نبوی دعا کی قوت پر اسی طرح بحث کی جیسے شیعہ ذرائع میں ہوئی۔ مومنوں کو صبر سے اصلاح کی کوششوں کو الہٰی مدد اور مداخلت کے لیے دعا کے ساتھ ملانا چاہیے کی تعلیم میں مشترکہ بنیاد ہے۔ دونوں روایات زور دیتی ہیں کہ حتمی فیصلہ اللہ کا ہے اور برائی کی ظاہری فتح عارضی ہے۔ عصری علماء تمام روایات میں ظلم یا وسیع پیمانے پر فساد کا سامنا کرنے والے مومنوں کو امید برقرار رکھنے اور الہٰی مدد کے لیے مسلسل دعا کرنے کی حوصلہ افزائی کرتے ہیں۔ اس بات پر اتفاق ہے کہ دعا غیر فعال استعفیٰ نہیں بلکہ الہٰی قوت کی فعال مشغولیت ہے، اور مخلص دعا الہٰی مداخلت لا سکتی ہے جو بظاہر ناممکن حالات کو بدل دیتی ہے۔ دونوں روایات حضرت لوط کی مختصر دعا کو بحران کے لمحات میں اللہ کی طرف رجوع کرنے اور الہٰی عدل پر اعتماد کرنے کے نمونے کے طور پر دیکھتی ہیں۔
30.layer4_ar: يُؤكِّد علماء الشيعة والسنة على السواء أن دعاء لوطٍ عليه السلام يُجسِّد التوكُّل الصحيح على الله في مواجهة المعارضة. ويُلاحِظ كلٌّ من ابن كثير والطباطبائي أن هذا الدعاء استُجيب بتدخُّلٍ إلهي فوري: أُرسِلت الملائكة لتدمير المجتمع المفسد. وثمة إجماعٌ على أن مصطلح «الْمُفْسِدِينَ» يُشير إلى أولئك الذين يبثُّون الفساد اجتماعيًّا لا فرديًّا فحسب، مما يُفاقِم إثمهم. ويُثني المفسِّرون الكلاسيكيون من الفريقَين على صبر لوطٍ عليه السلام في دعوة قومه وعلى لجوئه الأخير إلى الله طالبًا الحكم حين أبَوا الرجوع. ويُقرِّر الفريقان أن الدعاء بالنصر على الظالمين مشروعٌ وكثيرًا ما يُستجاب. ويُناقش الرازي قدرة الدعاء النبوي بأسلوبٍ مقارب لما في المصادر الشيعية. وثمة أرضية مشتركة في التعليم بأن على المؤمنين الجمعَ بين الصبر في الإصلاح وبين الدعاء لاستمداد العون الإلهي والتدخُّل الرباني. ويُؤكِّد الفريقان أن الحكم الأخير لله وحده، وأن انتصار الباطل الظاهر لا يعدو كونه مؤقَّتًا زائلاً. ويُشجِّع علماء الفريقَين المعاصرون المؤمنين الذين يواجهون الاضطهاد أو الفساد المتفشِّي على المثابرة في الرجاء والدعاء الدائم لاستمداد العون الإلهي. وثمة إجماعٌ على أن الدعاء ليس استسلامًا سلبيًّا بل استثمارٌ فاعل للقدرة الإلهية، وأن الابتهال الصادق قادرٌ على استجلاب تدخُّلٍ إلهي يُحوِّل الأحوال التي تبدو مستحيلة التغيير. ويرى الفريقان في دعاء لوطٍ الوجيز نموذجًا يُحتذى في اللجوء إلى الله لحظةَ الأزمات والثقة التامة بعدالة الله.
30.layer1: Verse 30 records one of the most moving moments in the Quranic account of Lot's mission: his prayer to Allah at the point when all human efforts to reform his community had been exhausted. After years of preaching, after being mocked and threatened, after watching his people not only refuse to reform but publicly challenge divine punishment, Lot turns to Allah with two words of supplication: 'Rabbi unsurni ala al-qawm al-mufsideen' — 'My Lord, help me against the corrupt people.' This brief but profound prayer captures the essence of prophetic trust in Allah. The word 'unsurni' — from nasr, meaning help or victory — is not a prayer for revenge but for divine justice and relief from ongoing oppression. The term 'al-mufsidun' — the corrupt, the spreaders of corruption — is the same root used throughout the Quran to describe those who actively damage the moral and social fabric of their communities. By using this description, Lot is not making a personal complaint but a moral assessment: these people are causing deep, widespread harm to themselves and to those around them. The timing of this prayer is significant: it comes after every other avenue has been tried, after the community's response has made clear that human persuasion alone cannot save them. This models a prophetic principle: believers exhaust the means available to them — advice, warning, patient repetition — and then place their trust entirely in Allah's power and timing. The brevity and directness of the supplication is itself instructive: Lot does not elaborate or explain to Allah, because Allah already knows. He simply turns, trusts, and asks. This verse has been a source of comfort for believers throughout history who face wickedness they cannot overcome through their own strength alone.
30.layer2: Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir al-Quran al-Azim explains that Lot's prayer immediately precedes the divine response recorded in verse 31, in which the angels arrive — having first visited Ibrahim — to inform Lot that divine punishment for his people has been decreed. The speed of the divine response, Ibn Kathir observes, demonstrates the Quranic principle that the prayer of a prophet against a community that has fulfilled all conditions for divine punishment is almost immediately answered. He cites similar patterns in the stories of Noah, whose prayer recorded in Surah Nuh was followed by the flood, and of Moses, whose prayer against Pharaoh was followed by divine confirmation that it had been accepted. Imam Tabari in his Jami al-Bayan records from scholars of the early generation including Mujahid and Qatada that the title 'al-mufsidun' in this supplication refers specifically to the total and comprehensive nature of the people's corruption — they did not merely err in one area but had corrupted their entire social, moral, and spiritual life. Al-Qurtubi in Al-Jami li-Ahkam al-Quran derives from this verse a number of legal and spiritual principles: that it is permitted to pray against oppressors; that labeling the corrupt as corrupt is not slander but truth; and that the prophet's patient endurance over many years before turning to this prayer demonstrates that such supplication for divine intervention should be a last resort after all legitimate means have been exhausted. Al-Razi notes the beauty of Lot's attribution of the request to his Lord — 'Rabbi' — emphasizing that even in the moment of crisis, Lot's relationship with Allah is one of intimate reliance and recognition of divine sovereignty over all outcomes.
30.layer3: Sayyid Qutb in Fi Zilal al-Quran writes that verse 30 represents the believer's ultimate resort: when truth has been proclaimed, patience has been maintained, and the community has responded only with mockery and challenge, the believing heart turns entirely to Allah. Qutb calls this the moment of 'prophetic tawakkul' — not passive resignation but the active entrusting of one's cause to the only power capable of resolving it. He notes that Lot's prayer is a model of spiritual maturity: he does not despair, become bitter, or abandon his position; he simply redirects his energy from human persuasion to divine supplication. Wahbah al-Zuhayli in Al-Tafsir al-Munir connects Lot's prayer to the broader Islamic ethic of responding to injustice: believers are obligated first to change wrongdoing with their hands if able, then with their tongues through speech, and finally with their hearts through prayer and rejection of the wrong — a hierarchy reflected in the famous hadith of the Prophet preserved in Sahih Muslim. This verse, al-Zuhayli notes, shows that the third level — dua and internal rejection of corruption — is not weakness but an expression of faith in divine justice. Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen draws a contemporary lesson: in situations where believers face organized opposition to truth that they cannot overcome through available means, turning to sincere dua is not abandoning the struggle but elevating it to its highest dimension. He also notes that calling corruption by its name — as Lot does with the term 'mufsidun' — is itself an act of moral clarity that contemporary believers must not shy away from, even in cultures that pressure people to relativize moral judgments. The verse ultimately affirms that divine justice will prevail, and that the believer's role is to maintain truthful testimony and sincere supplication until it does.

concepts.title: Good News First
concepts.coreInsight: The angels came to Abraham with good news before delivering news of destruction, showing divine mercy precedes justice.
concepts.whyItMatters: Allah's pattern is to combine mercy with justice - blessings for the righteous accompany warnings for the corrupt.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: فرشتے تباہی کی خبر دینے سے پہلے ابراہیم کے پاس خوشخبری لے کر آئے، جو ظاہر کرتا ہے کہ الہٰی رحمت انصاف سے پہلے آتی ہے۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: اللہ کا طریقہ رحمت کو انصاف کے ساتھ ملانا ہے - نیکوں کے لیے نعمتیں فاسدوں کے لیے تنبیہات کے ساتھ آتی ہیں۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: جاءت الملائكة إلى إبراهيم بالبشرى قبل إبلاغ أخبار الدمار، مما يظهر أن الرحمة الإلهية تسبق العدالة.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: نمط الله هو الجمع بين الرحمة والعدالة - البركات للصالحين تصاحب التحذيرات للفاسدين.

concepts.title: Decreed Destruction
concepts.coreInsight: The angels announced the certain destruction of Lot's city, showing that when divine patience ends, punishment becomes inevitable.
concepts.whyItMatters: There comes a point where societal corruption crosses a threshold and divine mercy gives way to divine justice.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: فرشتوں نے لوط کے شہر کی یقینی تباہی کا اعلان کیا، جو ظاہر کرتا ہے کہ جب الہٰی صبر ختم ہوتا ہے، سزا ناگزیر ہو جاتی ہے۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: ایک مقام آتا ہے جہاں سماجی بدعنوانی ایک حد کو عبور کر جاتی ہے اور الہٰی رحمت الہٰی انصاف میں بدل جاتی ہے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: أعلنت الملائكة عن الدمار المؤكد لمدينة لوط، مما يظهر أنه عندما ينتهي الصبر الإلهي، يصبح العقاب حتمياً.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: هناك نقطة يعبر فيها الفساد المجتمعي عتبة معينة وتفسح الرحمة الإلهية المجال للعدالة الإلهية.

concepts.title: The Wrongdoers
concepts.coreInsight: The people are described as 'wrongdoers' (zalimeen) - those who transgress against themselves, others, and divine law.
concepts.whyItMatters: Wrongdoing is not just breaking rules but harming oneself spiritually, others socially, and transgressing against the Creator.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: لوگوں کو 'ظالمین' کے طور پر بیان کیا گیا ہے - وہ جو اپنے، دوسروں اور الہٰی قانون کے خلاف زیادتی کرتے ہیں۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: ظلم صرف قواعد توڑنا نہیں ہے بلکہ اپنے آپ کو روحانی طور پر، دوسروں کو سماجی طور پر، اور خالق کے خلاف تجاوز کرنا ہے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: وُصف الناس بأنهم 'ظالمون' - أولئك الذين يتجاوزون ضد أنفسهم والآخرين والقانون الإلهي.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: الظلم ليس مجرد كسر القواعد بل إلحاق الضرر بالنفس روحياً، وبالآخرين اجتماعياً، والتعدي على الخالق.

31.layer4: Both Shia and Sunni scholars agree on the basic narrative of the angels visiting Abraham with news of Isaac's birth and Sodom's destruction, as recorded in Tabari's Jami al-Bayan and Tabrisi's Majma al-Bayan. However, there are nuanced differences in emphasis. Sunni commentators like Ibn Kathir focus primarily on the historical narrative and moral lessons about sexual transgression. Shia tafsir, particularly Al-Mizan, emphasizes the theological concept of divine mercy preceding wrath and the role of prophets as intercessors for their communities. Qurtubi's Al-Jami li-Ahkam al-Quran discusses legal implications regarding communal sin, aligning with Shia perspectives on collective responsibility. Fakhr al-Din al-Razi in Mafatih al-Ghayb explores the philosophical question of how angels take physical form, which Shia scholars address through their understanding of 'barzakh' (intermediate realm). Both traditions agree that the story serves as a warning against normalized immorality. The main consensus is that divine patience has limits when societies institutionalize transgression, though Shia tafsir uniquely connects this to the concept of guardianship and the responsibility of spiritual leadership to warn communities.
31.layer4_urdu: شیعہ اور سنی دونوں علماء فرشتوں کے حضرت ابراہیم علیہ السلام کے پاس اسحاق علیہ السلام کی ولادت اور سدوم کی تباہی کی خبر لے کر آنے کی بنیادی روایت پر متفق ہیں، جیسا کہ طبری کی جامع البیان اور طبرسی کی مجمع البیان میں درج ہے۔ تاہم تاکید میں باریک فرق موجود ہیں۔ ابن کثیر جیسے سنی مفسرین بنیادی طور پر تاریخی بیان اور جنسی انحراف کے اخلاقی سبق پر توجہ مرکوز کرتے ہیں۔ شیعہ تفسیر، خاص طور پر المیزان، اس الہٰیاتی تصور پر زور دیتی ہے کہ الہٰی رحمت عذاب سے پہلے آتی ہے اور انبیاء کا اپنی برادریوں کے لیے شفیع ہونے کا کردار۔ قرطبی کی الجامع لاحکام القرآن اجتماعی گناہ کے قانونی مضمرات پر بحث کرتی ہے، جو اجتماعی ذمہ داری پر شیعہ نقطہ نظر سے ہم آہنگ ہے۔ فخر الدین رازی مفاتیح الغیب میں اس فلسفیانہ سوال کو تلاش کرتے ہیں کہ فرشتے جسمانی شکل کیسے اختیار کرتے ہیں، جسے شیعہ علماء برزخ کی اپنی تفہیم کے ذریعے حل کرتے ہیں۔ دونوں روایات اس بات پر متفق ہیں کہ یہ قصہ معمول کی بے اخلاقی کے خلاف تنبیہ کے طور پر کام کرتا ہے، اگرچہ شیعہ تفسیر اسے روحانی قیادت کی ذمہ داری اور ولایت کے تصور سے منفرد طور پر جوڑتی ہے۔
31.layer4_ar: يتَّفقُ المفسِّرون الشِّيعةُ والسُّنَّةُ على أصلِ الرِّوايةِ المتعلِّقة بزيارةِ الملائكةِ لإبراهيمَ بخبرِ وِلادة إسحاقَ وهلاكِ سدوم، كما تُسجِّلُه «جامعُ البيان» للطَّبريِّ و«مجمعُ البيان» للطَّبرسيِّ. غيرَ أنَّ ثمَّةَ فوارق دقيقةً في التَّأكيدات: يُركِّزُ المفسِّرون السُّنَّة كابن كثيرٍ أساساً على السَّرديَّة التَّاريخيَّة والدُّروس الأخلاقيَّة المتعلِّقة بالتَّعدِّي الجنسيِّ، بينما يُشدِّدُ التَّفسيرُ الشِّيعيُّ، ولا سيَّما «الميزان»، على المفهوم العقديِّ بتقدُّمِ الرَّحمةِ على الغضب ودورِ الأنبياءِ شُفعاءَ لأقوامِهم. ويتناولُ القرطبيُّ في «الجامع لأحكام القرآن» التَّبعاتِ الشَّرعيَّةَ للذَّنبِ الجماعيِّ، منسجماً مع رُؤى التَّفسير الشِّيعيِّ في مسألةِ المسؤوليَّة الجماعيَّة. ويستكشفُ الرَّازيُّ في «مفاتيح الغيب» المسألةَ الفلسفيَّةَ المتعلِّقة بكيفيَّةِ تجسُّدِ الملائكة في هيئةٍ جسديَّة، وهو ما يُعالجُه العلماءُ الشِّيعةُ عبرَ فهمِهم لعالَم البرزخ. كلا التَّقليدَين يتَّفقان على أنَّ القصَّةَ تُمثِّل تحذيراً من الفُحشِ المُطبَّع في المجتمع، وإن كانت التَّفاسير الشِّيعيَّة تُضفي على ذلك بُعداً فريداً بربطِها بمفهوم الوَلاية ومسؤوليَّة القيادةِ الرُّوحيَّة في تحذيرِ الجماعات.
31.layer1: Verse 31 of Surah Al-Ankabut marks a dramatic shift in the narrative of Prophet Lut, as Allah's angels arrive first at the home of Prophet Ibrahim bearing two messages: glad tidings of a righteous son, and the solemn announcement of imminent destruction for the people of Lut's city. The phrase 'our messengers came to Ibrahim with glad tidings' connects this passage to the broader story found in Surah Hud and Surah Al-Hijr, where the angels first delivered the news of the birth of Ishaq and then revealed their mission to destroy Sodom. The Arabic word 'muhlikoo' meaning 'those who will destroy' conveys absolute divine certainty - this is not a conditional warning but a decree already in effect. The people are called 'zalimeen', meaning wrongdoers or oppressors, a term that encompasses transgression against oneself, against others, and against Allah's law. This verse teaches believers that divine mercy and divine justice operate together: the same messengers who bring glad tidings to the righteous also carry the sentence of punishment for the corrupt. The asbab al-nuzul context situates this passage within the Meccan period, reassuring the early Muslim community in Mecca that just as Lut's believing household was preserved amid the destruction of his people, the Prophet Muhammad and his companions would also be protected. The practical lesson is that living righteously within a corrupt society is possible and honoured by Allah, and that His knowledge of every individual's condition is perfect and complete.
31.layer2: Imam Tabari in his Jami al-Bayan records multiple narrations from the Companions and Successors about this verse, noting that the angels arrived at Ibrahim's home in human form, handsome young men, and first delivered the joyful news of a son before informing him of their destructive mission toward Sodom. Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir al-Quran al-Azim draws on these same narrations, citing the accounts of Ibn Abbas and Mujahid who explain that Ibrahim's reaction to the news of Sodom's destruction was to begin pleading on behalf of Lut's people, as Allah records in Surah Hud. Ibn Kathir emphasizes that the angels' statement 'we are the destroyers of the people of this city' uses the active participial construction 'muhlikoo' to convey the certainty and imminence of the divine decree, as though the destruction had already been completed in the divine plan. Al-Qurtubi in his Jami li-Ahkam al-Quran discusses the significance of the word 'zalimeen' applied to Lut's people, noting that classical scholars including Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak understood this to encompass all their sins collectively: their disbelief, their sexual transgression, their mistreatment of guests, and their mocking of the Prophet sent to them. Fakhr al-Din al-Razi in his Mafatih al-Ghayb raises the question of why the angels first visited Ibrahim rather than proceeding directly to Sodom, and offers the answer that this was a mercy to Ibrahim so that he would be at peace knowing his nephew Lut would be saved, and also so that Ibrahim's intercession could be recorded as evidence of the prophetic concern for humanity.
31.layer3: Wahbah al-Zuhayli in his Al-Tafsir al-Munir highlights the theological significance of the angels arriving with dual tidings in this verse: the birth of a new prophet to continue the chain of divine guidance and the end of a society that had rejected all guidance. He notes that this pairing reflects the Quranic law of replacement - when a community destroys itself through moral ruin, Allah preserves the mission of prophethood through a new line of righteous leadership. Sayyid Qutb in Fi Zilal al-Quran writes with characteristic depth that the angels arriving first at Ibrahim's door before going to Lut reveals the divine courtesy of informing the closest concerned party first, and that Ibrahim's immediate intercession for Lut's people shows the depth of prophetic compassion even toward those who do not deserve mercy. Ibn Uthaymeen, in his lessons on the stories of the prophets, draws attention to the description of Lut's people as 'wrongdoers' and points out that this single word encapsulates the totality of their moral collapse: they had wronged themselves by inverting the natural order of human sexuality, wronged their community by spreading corruption openly, and wronged the divine order by mocking Allah's messenger. Contemporary scholars also note that this verse demonstrates that divine punishment does not arrive arbitrarily but only after a full and fair opportunity for repentance has been exhausted, a principle that gives context to all the stories of destroyed nations in the Quran and reassures believers that Allah's justice is always proportionate and preceded by mercy.

concepts.title: Abraham's Care
concepts.coreInsight: Abraham's immediate concern for Lot shows the compassion prophets have for believers, even when surrounded by wrongdoers.
concepts.whyItMatters: True faith includes concern for the welfare of fellow believers, especially when they face danger or difficulty.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: لوط کے لیے ابراہیم کی فوری فکر انبیاء کی شفقت کو ظاہر کرتی ہے جو مومنین کے لیے ہوتی ہے، یہاں تک کہ جب وہ ظالموں سے گھرے ہوں۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: سچے ایمان میں ساتھی مومنین کی فلاح و بہبود کی فکر شامل ہے، خاص طور پر جب وہ خطرے یا مشکل کا سامنا کریں۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: يظهر اهتمام إبراهيم الفوري بلوط الرحمة التي يتمتع بها الأنبياء تجاه المؤمنين، حتى عندما يكونون محاطين بالظالمين.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: الإيمان الحقيقي يتضمن الاهتمام برفاهية المؤمنين الآخرين، خاصة عندما يواجهون الخطر أو الصعوبة.

concepts.title: We Know Better
concepts.coreInsight: The angels responded 'We know better who is within it' - affirming that Allah's knowledge is perfect and His plans are precise.
concepts.whyItMatters: Trusting Allah's knowledge and judgment is essential, even when we don't fully understand His decisions or timing.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: فرشتوں نے جواب دیا 'ہم بہتر جانتے ہیں کون اس میں ہے' - تصدیق کرتے ہوئے کہ اللہ کا علم کامل ہے اور اس کے منصوبے درست ہیں۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: اللہ کے علم اور فیصلے پر بھروسہ ضروری ہے، یہاں تک کہ جب ہم اس کے فیصلوں یا وقت کو پوری طرح نہیں سمجھتے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: أجابت الملائكة 'نحن أعلم بمن فيها' - مؤكدة أن علم الله كامل وخططه دقيقة.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: الثقة بعلم الله وحكمه ضرورية، حتى عندما لا نفهم قراراته أو توقيته بشكل كامل.

concepts.title: The Exception
concepts.coreInsight: Lot's wife was excluded from salvation because she supported the wrongdoers, showing that family ties don't guarantee salvation.
concepts.whyItMatters: Faith and righteousness, not family relationships, determine one's fate - even a prophet's wife can be among the lost.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: لوط کی بیوی کو نجات سے خارج کر دیا گیا کیونکہ اس نے ظالموں کی حمایت کی، جو ظاہر کرتا ہے کہ خاندانی تعلقات نجات کی ضمانت نہیں دیتے۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: ایمان اور نیکی، خاندانی رشتے نہیں، کسی کی قسمت کا تعین کرتے ہیں - یہاں تک کہ نبی کی بیوی بھی گمراہوں میں ہو سکتی ہے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: استُثنيت امرأة لوط من النجاة لأنها دعمت الظالمين، مما يظهر أن الروابط العائلية لا تضمن الخلاص.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: الإيمان والصلاح، وليس العلاقات العائلية، يحددان مصير المرء - حتى زوجة نبي يمكن أن تكون من الهالكين.

32.layer4: Both Shia and Sunni exegetes agree on the fundamental narrative that Lot's wife was excluded from salvation due to her inner alignment with the disbelievers. Ibn Kathir in his tafsir mentions narrations suggesting she would mock visitors and warn the townspeople. Tabari's Jami al-Bayan includes similar accounts of her betrayal. Where traditions differ is in emphasis: Sunni commentators often focus on her disobedience to her husband, while Shia scholars emphasize her betrayal of prophetic mission and divine guidance. Qurtubi discusses legal implications regarding marriage to disbelievers, similar to Shia jurisprudential discussions. Al-Razi explores philosophical questions about divine foreknowledge and human choice, asking how her fate could be predetermined while maintaining free will - a question Shia theology addresses through the concept of 'al-amr bayn al-amrayn' (the matter between two matters), where divine knowledge does not negate human agency. Both traditions derive the lesson that faith is individual responsibility transcending family ties. The consensus is clear: being married to a prophet or living in a righteous household provides opportunity but not automatic salvation.
32.layer4_urdu: شیعہ اور سنی دونوں مفسرین اس بنیادی بیان پر متفق ہیں کہ لوط علیہ السلام کی بیوی کو نجات سے خارج کیا گیا کیونکہ اس کا باطن کافروں کے ساتھ تھا۔ ابن کثیر نے اپنی تفسیر میں وہ روایات درج کی ہیں جن میں بتایا گیا ہے کہ وہ مہمانوں کا مذاق اڑاتی اور شہر والوں کو خبردار کرتی تھی۔ طبری کی جامع البیان میں اس کی غداری کے ایسے ہی واقعات موجود ہیں۔ جہاں روایات میں فرق ہے وہ تاکید میں ہے: سنی مفسرین اکثر اپنے شوہر کی نافرمانی پر زور دیتے ہیں جبکہ شیعہ علماء نبوی مشن اور الہٰی رہنمائی کے ساتھ غداری پر زور دیتے ہیں۔ قرطبی کافروں سے شادی کے بارے میں قانونی مضمرات پر بحث کرتے ہیں جو شیعہ فقہی مباحث سے ملتا جلتا ہے۔ رازی الہٰی پیش آگاہی اور انسانی انتخاب کے بارے میں فلسفیانہ سوالات کو تلاش کرتے ہیں اور پوچھتے ہیں کہ آزاد ارادے کو برقرار رکھتے ہوئے اس کا مقدر کیسے پیشگی متعین ہو سکتا ہے، جس کا شیعہ الہٰیات الامر بین الامرین یعنی دو معاملوں کے درمیان معاملہ کے تصور کے ذریعے جواب دیتی ہے۔ دونوں روایات یہ سبق اخذ کرتی ہیں کہ ایمان خاندانی رشتوں سے ماورا انفرادی ذمہ داری ہے۔
32.layer4_ar: يتَّفقُ المفسِّرون الشِّيعةُ والسُّنَّةُ على الرِّوايةِ الجوهريَّة من أنَّ زوجةَ لوط حُرِمَت من النَّجاة بسببِ موالاتِها الباطنيَّة للكافرين. وقد ذكرَ ابنُ كثيرٍ في تفسيرِه رواياتٍ تُشيرُ إلى أنَّها كانت تُخبِرُ أهلَ البلدةِ بقُدومِ الزُّوار، بما ينسجمُ مع رواياتِ «جامع البيان» للطَّبريِّ. أمَّا أوجهُ الاختلاف فهي في التَّأكيدات: يُركِّزُ المفسِّرون السُّنَّة في الغالبِ على عصيانِها لزوجِها، في حين يُشدِّدُ العلماءُ الشِّيعةُ على خيانتِها للرِّسالةِ النُّبويَّةِ والهُدى الإلهيِّ. ويتناولُ القرطبيُّ التَّبعاتِ الفقهيَّةَ للزَّواجِ من الكافرين، مُتقاطِعاً مع المناقشاتِ الفقهيَّةِ الشِّيعيَّة. ويستكشفُ الرَّازيُّ الإشكاليَّةَ الفلسفيَّةَ حول العِلمِ الإلهيِّ المُسبَق وحريَّةِ الاختيار، سائلاً كيفَ يُمكنُ أن يكونَ مصيرُها مُحدَّداً سلفاً مع الحفاظِ على الإرادة الحرَّة، وهو ما تُعالجُه اللاهوتُ الشِّيعيُّ عبرَ مفهوم «الأمرِ بين أمرَين» الذي لا ينفي فيه العِلمُ الإلهيُّ المُسبَقُ الاختيارَ الإنسانيَّ. وكلا التَّقليدَين يستخلصانِ الدَّرسَ نفسَه: الإيمانُ مسؤوليَّةٌ فرديَّة تتجاوزُ الروابطَ الأُسريَّة، والكونُ في بيتِ النَّبيِّ يُتيحُ الفرصةَ لكنَّه لا يُضمِنُ النَّجاة.
32.layer1: Verse 32 records the deeply human and compassionate response of Prophet Ibrahim upon hearing that the city would be destroyed: his immediate thought and spoken concern was for his nephew Lut who lived among the condemned people. 'Ibrahim said: But Lut is there!' This brief exclamation reveals the prophet's pure concern for a fellow believer isolated in a land of corruption. The angels' reply - 'We know better who is in it' - is a gentle affirmation of divine omniscience, assuring Ibrahim that Allah has already accounted for every righteous soul within the city and that His plan of salvation is precise and perfect. The angels confirmed they would save Lut and all of his household with one exception: his wife, who was condemned to remain with the destroyed. Classical scholars explain that Lut's wife had secretly aligned herself with the townspeople, would warn them of Lut's guests, and had abandoned her husband's mission in her heart. This verse carries profound lessons about individual accountability in faith: family membership and proximity to a prophet provide opportunity but not automatic salvation. Each soul stands alone before Allah on the basis of its own choices and loyalties. The verse also illustrates that Allah's divine plan accounts for every individual - not a single righteous person is overlooked or collateral damage in divine justice. For the early Muslim community facing persecution, this verse offered a powerful assurance that Allah knows who among them is sincere, and His protection extends precisely to those who deserve it.
32.layer2: Ibn Kathir in his commentary on this verse records narrations from Ibn Masud and Ibn Abbas explaining the precise nature of Lut's wife's betrayal. She would signal to the townspeople when strangers arrived at Lut's home, enabling the men of Sodom to gather and harm his guests. Ibn Kathir notes that the Quran in Surah Al-Tahrim uses both Lut's wife and Noah's wife as examples of how being married to a prophet provides no spiritual guarantee if the heart is opposed to the prophetic mission. Imam Tabari in his Jami al-Bayan records various scholarly opinions on the phrase 'kaanat min al-ghaabireen' meaning she was among those who remained behind, with scholars including Mujahid and Qatada explaining that this means she would be struck by the divine punishment along with the rest of the wicked city. Al-Qurtubi discusses the remarkable confidence of the angels' statement 'we know better who is in it' and explains that this is one of the clearest affirmations in the Quran of divine omniscience in relation to individual moral states - Allah knows not only who is physically present in a place but what is in their hearts and what they deserve. The Tafsir al-Jalalayn, authored by al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti, notes concisely that Ibrahim's concern for Lut moved him to intercede, but the angels' response redirected him from intercession to reassurance, since the divine decree regarding the corrupt was already sealed and unalterable.
32.layer3: Wahbah al-Zuhayli observes in his Al-Tafsir al-Munir that verse 32 presents a crucial distinction between geographical belonging and spiritual belonging. Lut's wife was physically present in the righteous household but spiritually aligned with the corrupt city - and it was her spiritual allegiance that determined her fate, not her marital status or physical location. This principle, al-Zuhayli notes, has enduring relevance for Muslim communities living as minorities within non-Muslim societies, where the question of genuine versus superficial belonging to the community of faith is existentially significant. Sayyid Qutb in Fi Zilal al-Quran reflects beautifully on Ibrahim's intercession as a model of prophetic mercy: he could not bear even the thought of one righteous soul being lost in the destruction, and his instinctive cry of 'but Lut is there' is the voice of a heart consumed by care for others. Qutb points out that this is the character that Allah chooses for prophethood - radical love for humanity even when humanity has rejected divine guidance. Ibn Uthaymeen in his scholarly teachings emphasizes that the angels' statement 'we know better who is in it' serves as a complete answer to any human anxiety about divine injustice: when we worry that the righteous might suffer in collective punishment, Allah's response is that His knowledge is perfect and His justice discriminating - no believer is lost in divine retribution meant for the corrupt.

concepts.title: Prophet's Anxiety
concepts.coreInsight: Lot felt distressed and helpless when the angels arrived in human form, fearing his people would harm these guests.
concepts.whyItMatters: Even prophets experience anxiety and fear, but they continue fulfilling their duty to protect others and uphold righteousness.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: جب فرشتے انسانی شکل میں آئے تو لوط پریشان اور بے بس محسوس ہوئے، اس خوف سے کہ ان کے لوگ ان مہمانوں کو نقصان پہنچائیں گے۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: یہاں تک کہ انبیاء بھی اضطراب اور خوف کا تجربہ کرتے ہیں، لیکن وہ دوسروں کی حفاظت اور نیکی کو برقرار رکھنے کی اپنی ذمہ داری پوری کرتے رہتے ہیں۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: شعر لوط بالضيق والعجز عندما وصلت الملائكة في شكل بشري، خوفاً من أن يؤذي قومه هؤلاء الضيوف.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: حتى الأنبياء يعانون من القلق والخوف، لكنهم يستمرون في أداء واجبهم لحماية الآخرين والحفاظ على الصلاح.

concepts.title: Divine Comfort
concepts.coreInsight: The angels comforted Lot with 'Fear not, nor grieve' - showing that divine support removes both present fear and future sorrow.
concepts.whyItMatters: When Allah sends help, He also sends reassurance - believers should trust that divine aid includes emotional and spiritual comfort.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: فرشتوں نے لوط کو تسلی دی 'نہ ڈرو اور نہ غم کرو' - ظاہر کرتے ہوئے کہ الہٰی مدد موجودہ خوف اور مستقبل کے غم دونوں کو دور کرتی ہے۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: جب اللہ مدد بھیجتا ہے، تو وہ تسلی بھی بھیجتا ہے - مومنین کو بھروسہ کرنا چاہیے کہ الہٰی امداد میں جذباتی اور روحانی سکون شامل ہے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: عزّت الملائكة لوط بـ'لا تخف ولا تحزن' - مما يظهر أن الدعم الإلهي يزيل الخوف الحاضر والحزن المستقبلي.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: عندما يرسل الله المساعدة، يرسل أيضاً الطمأنينة - يجب على المؤمنين الثقة بأن المعونة الإلهية تشمل الراحة العاطفية والروحية.

concepts.title: Promise of Safety
concepts.coreInsight: The angels promised to save Lot and his family, except his wife - demonstrating that Allah rescues the righteous from calamity.
concepts.whyItMatters: Believers can trust that Allah will protect them from harm when surrounded by corruption, though trials may still come.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: فرشتوں نے لوط اور ان کے خاندان کو بچانے کا وعدہ کیا، سوائے ان کی بیوی کے - ظاہر کرتے ہوئے کہ اللہ نیکوں کو آفت سے بچاتا ہے۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: مومن بھروسہ کر سکتے ہیں کہ اللہ انہیں نقصان سے بچائے گا جب وہ بدعنوانی سے گھرے ہوں، حالانکہ آزمائشیں پھر بھی آ سکتی ہیں۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: وعدت الملائكة بإنقاذ لوط وأهله، إلا امرأته - مما يدل على أن الله ينقذ الصالحين من الكارثة.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: يمكن للمؤمنين الثقة بأن الله سيحميهم من الأذى عندما يكونون محاطين بالفساد، رغم أن التجارب قد تأتي.

33.layer4: Both Shia and Sunni tafsir traditions agree on the basic narrative of Lot's distress and the angelic reassurance. Ibn Kathir and Tabari both describe Lot's fear that his people would assault his guests, consistent with Tabrisi's account. Where traditions differ is in theological emphasis: Sunni scholars like Qurtubi focus on the prohibition of homosexuality and Lot's role as defender of natural morality, while Shia commentators emphasize the broader principle of prophetic burden in carrying knowledge of both divine protection and community destruction. Al-Razi discusses the philosophical question of whether prophets experience fear, concluding that fear of harm to others while trusting in divine protection for oneself is compatible with prophetic courage - a view shared by Tabatabai. Both traditions derive legal rulings about protecting guests and defending honor from this passage. The consensus across Islamic scholarship is that Lot exemplifies moral courage in impossible circumstances, and that his emotional distress was appropriate response to witnessing potential violence. Shia tafsir uniquely emphasizes the repeated mention of Lot's wife as theological principle rather than narrative detail, highlighting individual accountability as central theme.
33.layer4_urdu: شیعہ اور سنی دونوں تفسیری روایات حضرت لوط علیہ السلام کی پریشانی اور فرشتوں کی تسلی کی بنیادی روایت پر متفق ہیں۔ ابن کثیر اور طبری دونوں نے حضرت لوط علیہ السلام کے اس خوف کو بیان کیا ہے کہ ان کی قوم ان کے مہمانوں پر حملہ کر سکتی ہے، جو طبرسی کی روایت سے ہم آہنگ ہے۔ جہاں روایات میں فرق ہے وہ الہٰیاتی تاکید میں ہے: سنی علماء جیسے قرطبی ہم جنس پرستی کی ممانعت اور فطری اخلاقیات کے محافظ کے طور پر حضرت لوط علیہ السلام کے کردار پر توجہ مرکوز کرتے ہیں، جبکہ شیعہ مفسرین الہٰی حفاظت اور قومی تباہی کا علم رکھتے ہوئے نبوی بوجھ کے وسیع تر اصول پر زور دیتے ہیں۔ رازی اس فلسفیانہ سوال پر بحث کرتے ہیں کہ آیا انبیاء خوف محسوس کرتے ہیں اور اس نتیجے پر پہنچتے ہیں کہ دوسروں کے لیے نقصان کا خوف جبکہ اپنے لیے الہٰی حفاظت پر اعتماد نبوی ہمت سے مطابقت رکھتا ہے، یہ نقطہ نظر طباطبائی کے ساتھ مشترک ہے۔ دونوں روایات اس قصے سے مہمانوں کی حفاظت اور آبرو کی دفاع کے قانونی احکام اخذ کرتی ہیں۔ اتفاق واضح ہے کہ حضرت لوط علیہ السلام ناممکن حالات میں اخلاقی جرات کی مثال ہیں۔
33.layer4_ar: يتَّفقُ مفسِّرو الشِّيعةِ والسُّنَّةِ على جوهرِ الرِّوايةِ المتعلِّقة بكَرَبِ لوطٍ واطمئنانِ الملائكة له. ويصفُ ابنُ كثيرٌ والطَّبريُّ كلاهما خوفَ لوطٍ من أن يعتديَ قومُه على ضيوفِه بما ينسجمُ مع رواية الطَّبرسيِّ. وتتَّفقُ التَّقاليدُ العِلميَّةُ في تفسيرِ عبارةِ «لا تَخَف ولا تحزَن» بوصفِها دليلاً على الشَّجاعةِ النُّبويَّةِ في المواقفِ البالغةِ الصُّعوبة. غيرَ أنَّ المفسِّرين يَفترقون في التَّأكيدات؛ فيُركِّزُ علماءُ السُّنَّة كالقرطبيِّ على حُرمةِ الضَّيافةِ وواجبِ الدِّفاعِ عن الشَّرف، في حين يُشدِّدُ المفسِّرون الشِّيعةُ على المبدأِ الأشملِ لحِملِ النُّبوَّةِ في التَّعاملِ مع علمِ الحمايةِ الإلهيَّة وهلاكِ الجماعة في آنٍ واحد. ويبحثُ الرَّازيُّ المسألةَ الفلسفيَّةَ هل يعيشُ الأنبياءُ الخوف، فيخلصُ إلى أنَّ الخوفَ على الآخرين مع الثِّقةِ بحمايةِ الله للنَّفسِ لا يتعارضُ مع الشَّجاعةِ النُّبويَّة، وهو رأيٌ يُشاركُه الطَّباطبائيُّ. ويستنبطُ كلا التَّقليدَين أحكاماً شرعيَّةً تتعلَّقُ بحمايةِ الضَّيفِ والدِّفاعِ عن العِرض من هذا المقطع. والإجماعُ قائمٌ على أنَّ لوطاً يُجسِّدُ الشَّجاعةَ الأخلاقيَّةَ في مستحيلِ الظُّروف.
33.layer1: Verse 33 records one of the most psychologically vivid moments in the Quran: the arrival of the angels at Lut's home in the guise of handsome young men, and Lut's immediate anguish. The Arabic phrase 'saa-a bihim wa daaqa bihim dhara'an' conveys layered distress - he was pained by their arrival and felt his capacity to protect them utterly insufficient. Classical scholars explain that Lut's unique suffering was born of a terrible dilemma: as a prophet of hospitality, he was bound to receive these guests; but knowing his people's vile habits, he feared terribly for what would happen to these apparently human visitors. He did not yet know they were angels and therefore could not be harmed. This moment of prophetic vulnerability - a man of God reduced to helplessness and grief in the face of impossible circumstances - is presented in the Quran without apology, showing that faith does not immunize prophets from human anguish. The angels' response came swiftly: 'Do not fear, and do not grieve.' These two negations address both present anxiety and forward-looking sorrow - the fear of what the people might do, and the grief over the destruction that was coming. They then repeated the promise of salvation for Lut and his family, again excepting his wife. The verse teaches that divine help often arrives in the darkest moment of helplessness, and that angelic reassurance 'la takhaf wa la tahzan' is itself a form of divine mercy accompanying divine power.
33.layer2: Imam Tabari records in his Jami al-Bayan that the phrase 'saa-a bihim' is understood by classical scholars including Mujahid, Qatada, and al-Suddi as expressing Lut's profound distress and grief at their arrival, because he knew what his people would attempt when they saw such handsome young men as guests. Ibn Kathir elaborates in his Tafsir al-Quran al-Azim that Lut initially tried to discourage the angels from entering the city, walking slowly ahead of them and speaking to them in veiled terms to dissuade them, hoping they would turn back before reaching his home - all of this because his people had terrorized him with their actions for years. Ibn Kathir also notes the linguistic richness of 'daaqa bihim dhara'an' meaning his capacity or arm became narrow on their account, an Arabic idiom expressing utter helplessness - a man who feels he has no room to maneuver, no means of protection, no resource available. The Tafsir al-Jalalayn notes that the angels' command 'la takhaf wa la tahzan' addresses two distinct emotional states: khawf or fear relates to something anticipated in the future, while huzn or grief relates to something already troubling in the present - the angels addressed both dimensions of Lut's emotional state with a single elegant dual command. Al-Qurtubi in his comprehensive commentary draws out the jurisprudential implication that a Muslim host has a duty of protection over his guests and that the failure to protect is a source of genuine grief, establishing the sanctity of hospitality as a religious obligation in Islamic law.
33.layer3: Sayyid Qutb writes memorably in Fi Zilal al-Quran about this verse, noting that the image of Lut - a prophet of Allah reduced to paralyzed grief by his guests' arrival - is among the most human portraits in the entire Quran. Qutb observes that Allah preserves these moments of prophetic weakness not to diminish the prophets but to console ordinary believers: if a chosen prophet of Allah can feel utterly helpless and overwhelmed, then the believer who is crushed by circumstances beyond their control is not failing in faith - they are simply being human. The divine mercy in this verse, Qutb argues, lies precisely in how quickly the relief comes: before Lut's distress could deepen into despair, the angels revealed themselves and banished both his fear and his grief. Wahbah al-Zuhayli in Al-Tafsir al-Munir draws a contemporary application from the angels' dual reassurance 'do not fear, do not grieve': he argues that Islamic spiritual development should produce a person whose fear of the future and grief over the past are both transformed by trust in Allah, and that the prophetic experience of reassurance models the psychological station that every believer should aspire to reach through tawakkul or complete reliance on God. Muhammad al-Sha'rawi, in his celebrated lectures on this passage, observed that the angels came to Lut as human-seeming guests specifically to test whether his hospitality and righteousness would hold under the most difficult conditions imaginable - and that his distress, far from being a failure, was actually the supreme expression of his moral seriousness.

concepts.title: Heavenly Punishment
concepts.coreInsight: The punishment came from the sky, symbolizing divine origin - not a natural disaster but direct intervention from Allah.
concepts.whyItMatters: Some calamities are direct divine responses to moral corruption, serving as warnings to humanity across time.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: عذاب آسمان سے آیا، جو الہٰی منبع کی علامت ہے - کوئی قدرتی آفت نہیں بلکہ اللہ کی طرف سے براہ راست مداخلت۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: کچھ آفات اخلاقی بدعنوانی کے لیے براہ راست الہٰی ردعمل ہیں، جو وقت کے ساتھ انسانیت کے لیے تنبیہ کے طور پر کام کرتی ہیں۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: جاء العقاب من السماء، رمزاً للأصل الإلهي - ليس كارثة طبيعية بل تدخل مباشر من الله.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: بعض الكوارث هي استجابات إلهية مباشرة للفساد الأخلاقي، تعمل كتحذيرات للبشرية عبر الزمن.

concepts.title: Defiant Rebellion
concepts.coreInsight: The punishment came 'because they have been defiantly disobedient' - emphasizing the active, persistent nature of their rebellion.
concepts.whyItMatters: There's a difference between occasional sin and defiant, persistent rejection of divine guidance - the latter brings severe consequences.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: عذاب آیا 'کیونکہ وہ سرکشی سے نافرمان تھے' - ان کی بغاوت کی فعال، مستقل نوعیت پر زور دیتے ہوئے۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: کبھی کبھار گناہ اور الہٰی رہنمائی کی سرکش، مستقل مسترد کے درمیان فرق ہے - بعد والا شدید نتائج لاتا ہے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: جاء العقاب 'بما كانوا يفسقون' - مع التأكيد على الطبيعة النشطة والمستمرة لتمردهم.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: هناك فرق بين الخطيئة العرضية والرفض المتحدي المستمر للهداية الإلهية - الأخيرة تجلب عواقب وخيمة.

concepts.title: Complete Destruction
concepts.coreInsight: The entire city was targeted, not just individuals - showing how collective corruption brings collective punishment.
concepts.whyItMatters: Societal sins have societal consequences - when a community collectively embraces evil, divine punishment can be comprehensive.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: پورے شہر کو نشانہ بنایا گیا، نہ کہ صرف افراد کو - ظاہر کرتے ہوئے کہ اجتماعی بدعنوانی اجتماعی سزا لاتی ہے۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: سماجی گناہوں کے سماجی نتائج ہوتے ہیں - جب کوئی معاشرہ اجتماعی طور پر برائی کو اپناتا ہے، تو الہٰی سزا جامع ہو سکتی ہے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: استُهدفت المدينة بأكملها، وليس الأفراد فقط - مما يظهر كيف يجلب الفساد الجماعي عقاباً جماعياً.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: للخطايا المجتمعية عواقب مجتمعية - عندما يتبنى مجتمع الشر بشكل جماعي، يمكن أن يكون العقاب الإلهي شاملاً.

34.layer4: Both Shia and Sunni scholars agree on the historical destruction of Sodom through divine punishment. Ibn Kathir describes stones of baked clay striking each individual sinner, similar to Tabrisi's account. Tabari's Jami al-Bayan provides detailed descriptions of the punishment's nature, consistent with Shia sources. Where traditions differ is in theological interpretation: Sunni commentators like Qurtubi derive specific legal rulings about capital punishment for homosexuality from this verse, while Shia scholars emphasize broader principles of divine justice and the conditions under which communities face collective judgment. Al-Razi explores the philosophical tension between divine mercy and justice, asking why entire populations were destroyed - he concludes that when corruption becomes total and persistent, punishment serves universal benefit. Shia theology addresses this through the concept that divine actions serve ultimate wisdom beyond immediate human understanding. Both traditions agree that 'yafsuqun' indicates deliberate, persistent rejection of prophetic guidance. The consensus is that this historical event serves as permanent warning against institutionalizing immorality, though interpretations differ on specific applications to contemporary situations.
34.layer4_urdu: شیعہ اور سنی دونوں علماء الہٰی عذاب کے ذریعے سدوم کی تاریخی تباہی پر متفق ہیں۔ ابن کثیر پکی مٹی کے پتھروں کا ذکر کرتے ہیں جو ہر انفرادی گنہگار پر پڑے، جو طبرسی کی روایت سے مطابقت رکھتا ہے۔ طبری کی جامع البیان عذاب کی نوعیت کی تفصیلی وضاحت فراہم کرتی ہے جو شیعہ مصادر سے ہم آہنگ ہے۔ جہاں روایات میں فرق ہے وہ الہٰیاتی تشریح میں ہے: قرطبی جیسے سنی مفسرین اس آیت سے ہم جنس پرستی کے لیے سزاے موت کے مخصوص قانونی احکام اخذ کرتے ہیں، جبکہ شیعہ علماء الہٰی انصاف کے وسیع تر اصولوں اور ان حالات پر زور دیتے ہیں جن میں قومیں اجتماعی فیصلے کا سامنا کرتی ہیں۔ رازی رحمت اور عدل کے درمیان فلسفیانہ کشمکش کو تلاش کرتے ہیں اور پوچھتے ہیں کہ کیوں پوری آبادیاں تباہ کی گئیں، اور اس نتیجے پر پہنچتے ہیں کہ جب فساد مکمل اور مسلسل ہو جائے تو عذاب عالمگیر مفاد کی خدمت کرتا ہے۔ شیعہ الہٰیات اس کا جواب اس تصور کے ذریعے دیتی ہے کہ الہٰی اقدامات فوری انسانی فہم سے ماورا حتمی حکمت کی خدمت کرتے ہیں۔ دونوں روایات اس بات پر متفق ہیں کہ یَفسُقون نبوی رہنمائی کو جان بوجھ کر اور مسلسل رد کرنے کی نشاندہی کرتا ہے۔
34.layer4_ar: يتَّفقُ مفسِّرو الشِّيعةِ والسُّنَّةِ على الهلاكِ التَّاريخيِّ لسدوم بعذابٍ إلهيٍّ. ويصفُ ابنُ كثيرٌ حجارةَ الطِّينِ المُحرَقِ التي أصابَت كلَّ مذنبٍ بعينِه بما يتَّفقُ مع ما أوردَه الطَّبرسيُّ. والرِّواياتُ في «جامع البيان» للطَّبريِّ تُقدِّمُ تصويراً مُفصَّلاً لطبيعةِ العذابِ يتَّسقُ مع المصادرِ الشِّيعيَّة. ومواطنُ الاختلافِ تكمنُ في التَّفسيرِ العقديِّ: فالمفسِّرون السُّنَّة كالقرطبيِّ يستنبطون من هذه الآيةِ أحكاماً شرعيَّةً تتعلَّقُ بالحدِّ على المثليَّة، في حين يُركِّزُ علماءُ الشِّيعةِ على مبادئِ العدلِ الإلهيِّ الأشملِ وشروطِ مساءلةِ المجتمعاتِ جماعيَّاً. ويستكشفُ الرَّازيُّ التَّوتُّرَ الفلسفيَّ بين الرَّحمةِ الإلهيَّةِ والعدل، سائلاً لمَ أُهلِكَت مجموعاتٌ بأكملِها، مُجيباً بأنَّه حين يصبحُ الفسادُ شاملاً ومُستمرَّاً يغدو العذابُ نفعاً عامَّاً للبشريَّة. واللاهوتُ الشِّيعيُّ يُعالجُ هذا عبرَ مفهوم أنَّ الأفعالَ الإلهيَّةَ تخدمُ حكمةً كُلِّيَّةً تتجاوزُ المفهومَ البشريَّ الآنيَّ. ويتَّفقُ كلا التَّقليدَين على أنَّ «يَفسُقون» يدلُّ على رفضٍ متعمَّدٍ ومتواصلٍ للهدايةِ النُّبويَّة، وأنَّ هذه الحادثةَ التَّاريخيَّة تُمثِّلُ تحذيراً دائماً من تأسيسِ الفُحشِ في مؤسَّساتِ المجتمع.
34.layer1: Verse 34 contains the angels' direct announcement of the divine punishment decreed for the people of Sodom: 'Indeed, we are going to bring down upon the people of this city a punishment from the sky because they have been defiantly disobedient.' The phrase 'rijzan min al-sama' meaning punishment or filth from the sky points to the divine origin of the catastrophe - this was not a natural event but a direct act of Allah. Classical tafsir scholars describe the punishment as a rain of stones of baked clay, as detailed in related verses in Surah Hud, which struck each individual sinner personally and destroyed the entire city.
